inlines.v: CALCINATION, noun [from calcine.] 1. The operation of expelling from a substance by heat, some volatile matter with which it is combined, or which is the cementing principle, and thus reducing it to a friable state. Thus chalk and carbonate of lime are reduced to lime by calcination or the expulsion of carbonic acid. 2. The operation of reducing a metal to an oxyd, or metallic calx. This is modern chemistry is called oxidation.
